name: Sonotube
seoDesc: Sonotube: work out sonotube® size from the height and the weight. A free construction calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: The Sonotube calculator turns the height, the weight and more into sonotube® size. That makes it useful for a materials order or a planning estimate you want to get roughly right first time. The unit chips sit next to the boxes, which is where most hand-calculation mistakes start.

sections.title: How does the Sonotube calculator work?
sections.html:
The Sonotube calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports sonotube® size in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the concrete mix and the concrete mix ratio); then you type in the height, the weight, the bag size and the bags needed.

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Sonotube calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Sonotube® size=2 × the square root of (volume ÷ (height × quantity)) ÷ the square root of (PI)
Concrete density=weight ÷ volume
Waste=(bag size × bags needed − weight) ÷ weight
Total concrete cost=bags needed × cost of each bag of pre-mix concrete
Total concrete cost=cost of concrete per unit volume × volume
Total concrete cost=cost per column × quantity

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

  • Length, opening in meters
  • Volume, opening in cubic meters
  • Density, opening in kilograms per cubic meter
  • Mass, opening in kilograms
  • Mass, opening in kilograms
  • %, opening in percent
  • Volume, opening in cubic meters
  • Volume, opening in cubic meters

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Sonotube calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Checking a supplier's figure against your own measurements
  • Ordering material and not wanting a second trip
  • Quoting a job where areas and quantities drive the price
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the height, the weight and the bag size — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Sonotube calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns sonotube® size, derived from the height, the weight and the bag size. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Sonotube calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the height, the weight, the bag size and the bags needed, which is 12 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter height in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Height opens in meters and the chip beside it offers 34 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (3 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Cc = 0. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Sonotube calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
